title: 2026 Ohio U.S. Senate special election
description: Ohio’s 2026 special U.S. Senate election will decide the remainder of the term that opened when J.D. Vance resigned to become vice president. The race is notable because Republicans are defending a seat in a state that has become more competitive but has leaned Republican in recent federal elections. Former Sen. Sherrod Brown is seeking a return to the Senate, while appointed Sen. Jon Husted is the GOP nominee, making the contest a key test of each party’s strength in Ohio.
polling_note: No public polling found for this race in the last 90 days as of 2026-05-08.

candidates.name: Jon Husted
candidates.summary: Jon Husted is a Republican U.S. senator from Ohio who began serving in January 2025 after being appointed to fill a vacancy. Before joining the Senate, he served as Ohio’s lieutenant governor, secretary of state, and a state legislator, and he also worked in economic development in the Dayton area.

candidates.donor_summary: Jon Husted’s 2025–2026 Senate committee had raised about $10.5M by April 15, 2026, with most money coming from individual contributions ($4.29M) and transfers from other authorized committees ($4.40M). flags.concern: The polling_note states 'No public polling found for this race in the last 90 days as of 2026-05-08,' but three polls are listed in the polling array, including one dated 2026-03-08 (61 days before the note date). March 8 falls within 90 days of May 8. This is an internal inconsistency — the note contradicts the data in the same profile.
flags.suggestion: Either remove the polling_note (since recent polling exists), or clarify that no polling was found after March 8, 2026 (i.e., in the last ~60 days). The note as written is factually inconsistent with the profile's own polling entries.

flags.concern: The FEC link for Jeffrey Kanter (candidates[2]) uses URL https://www.fec.gov/data/candidate/S6OH00395/ but the link title reads 'LEVY, GREGORY LEE - Candidate overview - FEC'. The same FEC ID (S6OH00395) is also used for Gregory Levy (candidates[3]), suggesting the FEC ID and/or link title is misassigned for Kanter. These two candidates cannot share the same FEC candidate ID.
flags.suggestion: Verify the correct FEC candidate ID for Jeffrey Kanter separately from Gregory Levy. The donor_source_url for Kanter also uses S6OH00395 — at least one of these assignments is incorrect and requires human verification against FEC records.

flags.concern: Gregory Levy's donor_source_url also uses https://www.fec.gov/data/candidate/S6OH00395/, and his donor_summary references this ID with financial figures ($57,814.65). If this ID is correctly Levy's, then the same ID listed under Kanter (candidates[2]) is erroneous. If it is Kanter's, then Levy's financials are misattributed. The duplication of FEC ID S6OH00395 across two different candidates is a clear data integrity issue.
flags.suggestion: Confirm which candidate holds FEC ID S6OH00395 and assign a separate, verified FEC ID to the other candidate.

flags.concern: The second source URL for Sherrod Brown's abortion stance (https://www.plannedparenthoodaction.org/planned-parenthood-advocates-ohio/media/planned-parenthood-advocates-ohio-announces-endorsement-of-sherrod-brown-for-reelection-to-the-us-senate-in-2026) includes the phrase 'reelection' in the URL slug. Brown is not running for reelection to his former seat — this is a special election for the seat vacated by J.D. Vance. The URL phrasing may reflect a Planned Parenthood editorial choice, but the profile description elsewhere correctly frames this as a special election. This is worth flagging for a human reviewer to confirm the URL resolves correctly and that the endorsement is genuine.
flags.suggestion: Verify the URL resolves to a valid Planned Parenthood endorsement page and note in the profile, if relevant, that this is a special election rather than a standard reelection campaign.

flags.concern: Jon Husted's education lists a Bachelor of Arts from the University of Dayton in 1989 and a Master of Arts also from the University of Dayton in 1993. My training data suggests Husted received his BA around 1989, which is plausible. However, the gap between 1989 and 1993 for an MA from the same institution is worth a human spot-check against the cited Bioguide or official Senate bio, as the degree year and field (political science for both) should be confirmed.
flags.suggestion: Cross-check against https://bioguide.congress.gov/search/bio/H001104 or https://www.husted.senate.gov/about/ to confirm the MA year and field are accurately represented.

flags.concern: The summary for Jeffrey Kanter states he 'would still appear on the ballot even though votes for him would not be counted,' while the withdrawal_reason field says he was 'removed from the ballot challenge process' and 'would not appear on the May primary ballot.' These two statements are not necessarily contradictory (he may appear on the general ballot but not the primary), but the relationship between the primary ballot exclusion and the general election ballot status is ambiguous and could confuse readers.
flags.suggestion: Clarify whether Kanter appears on the November general election ballot or not. If the disqualification means he does not appear at all, revise the summary accordingly. If he appears only on the general ballot but not the primary, make that distinction explicit.

flags.concern: Kanter is marked withdrawn: true, but the summary says 'votes for him would not be counted' while still suggesting he may appear on the ballot. A candidate who appears on the ballot — even if votes are not counted — may not be accurately described as 'withdrawn.' The term 'withdrawn' typically implies voluntary exit, whereas Kanter was disqualified.
flags.suggestion: Consider replacing 'withdrawn: true' with a more accurate status field such as 'disqualified: true' or adding a note that the candidate was involuntarily removed rather than voluntarily withdrawn.

flags.concern: Minor framing note: Brown's abortion stance is described as supporting 'federal protections for abortion and contraception and opposition to bans and restrictions.' This is accurate and neutral. However, for consistency with Husted's abortion section (which uses the phrase 'exceptions for rape, incest, or to save the life of the mother'), Brown's section could similarly note his position on specific procedural aspects of abortion rights, if available. The asymmetry is minor but worth flagging for completeness.
flags.suggestion: If Brown's campaign materials specify the scope of reproductive rights he supports (e.g., up to viability, throughout pregnancy), consider adding that detail to match the specificity offered for Husted.

flags.concern: The donor_summary references '2024 cycle fundraising was much larger, at about $93.7M raised.' This figure likely refers to Brown's 2024 regular Senate re-election campaign (which he lost to Bernie Moreno), not the current 2026 special election. The profile appropriately separates 2024 and 2025-2026 cycle data, but readers could potentially misread the $93.7M as relevant to the current race. The OpenSecrets URL for the 2024 data should be confirmed to ensure it refers to the correct cycle.
flags.suggestion: Add a parenthetical clarification that the $93.7M figure is from Brown's 2024 regular Senate re-election campaign, not the current 2026 special election.

flags.concern: Husted's climate stance mentions 'incentivize methane capture from coal mines' as part of an 'all-of-the-above' energy approach. The framing is accurate and neutral, but the profile does not mention any position on climate change itself (mitigation, emissions targets, etc.), only energy production. This is not a bias issue but a completeness gap — his Senate page sources are cited and may not have additional climate-specific content.
flags.suggestion: If Husted has taken any public position on climate science or emissions policy (separate from energy production), consider adding it. If not, the current framing with 'high' confidence based on available sources is acceptable.

flags.concern: Bill Redpath's healthcare stance is listed as 'No public position found' with low confidence, citing his campaign FAQ page. Given that Redpath is a longtime Libertarian activist with a campaign FAQ, it is plausible that his general Libertarian philosophy implies a market-based healthcare position, but the profile appropriately declines to infer from ideology. This is acceptable under the missing data policy.
flags.suggestion: No change required — the 'no public position found' approach is correct here. Human reviewer may wish to spot-check https://billredpath.com/faq/ to confirm healthcare is not addressed.

flags.concern: The race description says Ohio 'has become more competitive but has leaned Republican in recent federal elections.' This is a reasonable characterization but slightly editorializes about Ohio's political trajectory. 'Has become more competitive' implies a directional trend that could be contested depending on the time frame examined.

reviews.summary: This profile is broadly well-researched, with strong sourcing from official Senate pages, FEC data, Ballotpedia, and credible news outlets across most candidates. Issue stances for Husted and Levy are particularly well-documented with high-confidence citations from primary sources. However, several issues require attention: a potentially mislabeled FEC link for Kanter, an internal inconsistency in the polling_note vs. actual polling data, a description of Sherrod Brown's party label as 'reelection' when this is technically a special election for a different seat, minor asymmetric framing between candidates, and a factual concern about Husted's education timeline that should be verified.

flags.concern: The profile states no public position was found, which is accurate based on the provided sources; however, given the broad scope of this election, this is a notable, albeit acceptable, gap.

The donor summary for Jeffrey Kanter notes that federal campaign finance data was not clearly surfaced; given his status as a disqualified candidate, this is acceptable, but could be clarified by stating that no active committee is currently filing standard reports.
flags.suggestion: Clarify that the candidate's disqualification likely impacts the availability of standard FEC reporting metrics.

flags.concern: The summary notes difficulty in surfacing finance data for Bill Redpath. While the FEC links are provided, a concise summary of his current financial standing would improve completeness.
flags.suggestion: If data is unavailable due to the scale of the campaign, explicitly state that the campaign does not meet the threshold for extensive FEC reporting.
